description: Indianised coastal kingdom of central Vietnam (192–1832) whose Hindu and later Muslim rulers competed with the Vietnamese Đại Việt for control of the Indochinese coast; Cham sailors dominated South China Sea trade and Cham sculptural tradition, visible in the My Son sanctuary, represents the finest Hindu monumental art of mainland Southeast Asia; gradual Vietnamese southward expansion ultimately absorbed Cham territory.

lifecycle_phases.description: Cham kingdom of Lâm Ấp emerges from Chinese collapse in the south; Indianised court culture adopted; Hindu temple construction begins
Multiple Cham kingdoms, Panduranga, Kauthara, Amaravati, control central Vietnamese coast; My Son sanctuary at height; maritime trade flourishing
Vietnamese Đại Việt advance southward; Cham sacks Hanoi (1371) but cannot prevent Vietnamese colonisation; Vijaya capital taken (1471)
Champa reduced to rump state in Panduranga; slow Vietnamese absorption; final sultanate extinguished

rise_factors.description: Cham ports controlled the coastal trade route between the South China Sea and the Gulf of Thailand, collecting duties from East-West maritime traffic

decline_factors.description: Vietnamese demographic and agricultural expansion down the coast could not be reversed by Cham military resistance; slow attrition defeated Cham political autonomy
